name: Short Doubleedge
description: Lift the greataxe overhead with both hands and drop the bit straight down onto the target.

name: Quick Riven
description: Roll the head over the shoulder after a miss and bring it back across in a second cut.

name: Folded Haftbell
description: Slide the lead hand down the haft and raise the shaft to knock a thrust aside.

name: Riventrot
description: Plant the rear heel and drag the front foot forward one short step while holding the axe low.

name: Gentle Wideswell
description: Count the opponent's breaths from a steady guard to learn when the next attack is likely to come.

name: Poleshoe Hit
description: Grip high under the head and chop short and fast at close range where a full swing cannot fit.

name: Hard Sunder
description: Turn the axe over and drive the butt knob into the opponent's ribs or gut.

name: Greatdash
description: Switch the lead hand mid-swing so the cut lands from the opposite side of the body.

name: Axepause
description: Hold the haft level across the chest with both hands to stop a downward blow.

name: Light Greatbeard
description: Turn on the ball of the front foot to carry the body out of a line of attack.

name: Calm Greatpoll
description: Resettle both hands on the haft after a stroke and feel for slack or twist in the grip.

name: Sunderbump
description: Drive the hips around first so the shoulders and the axe head follow in a full horizontal swing.

name: Rend Drop
description: Arch the back to load the axe behind the head then fall forward into a long downward cut.

name: Haftrope Strike
description: Swing the head along the ground line to cut at the legs of a standing opponent.

name: Gnawing Longhelve
description: Sweep the bit up from low on one side to high on the other and catch the chin or arm.

name: Greatpace
description: Plant the lead foot to arrest the momentum of the swing and stand ready to strike again.

name: Tight Heavyeye
description: Carry the head low and close behind the lead leg so the shaft covers the knee and thigh.

name: Judging Greatbit
description: Count the beats of each full swing aloud so the body learns exactly how long a stroke takes.

name: Blunt Overhew
description: Spread the feet past the shoulders and chop with the full bit while the stance stays level.

name: Rivenhit
description: Turn a quarter circle on both feet and hew across the target's flank as the turn ends.

name: Quiet Splitmass
description: Slide each foot a hand's width at a time to close or open distance without lifting either foot.

name: Folded Greatbit
description: Bend the front knee and brace the haft against the thigh to absorb a heavy blow.

name: Even Haftrope
description: Feel through the soles of both feet for the opponent's weight shifting before an attack begins.

name: Short Hewfall
description: Heave the axe straight up with locked elbows and let its weight fall onto the target.

name: Gnawing Sunder
description: Shorten the swing when the arms tire and chop from the elbows with the weight of the head.

name: Stiff Poleshoe
description: Pull the bit back along the target by walking the hands down the haft in a drawing cut.

name: Backward Splitmass
description: Rest the haft on one shoulder and move at pace so the weapon arrives ready to swing.

name: Sunderhop
description: Shift the weight of the axe from one shoulder to the other while stepping to keep the stride even.

name: Doubleedge Lid
description: Ground the head and stand behind the upright haft so the shaft covers the body's front line.

name: Axebump
description: Cut a slanting notch into the front of the target with a downward diagonal stroke.

name: Single Greatpoll
description: Follow the notch cut from the opposite side with a level stroke to finish the felling.

name: Narrow Overhew
description: Bring the bit down along the grain of the target with the full weight of the body behind it.

name: Chopping Greatbeard
description: Land several short chops in the same spot to open a wound that a single stroke would not.

name: Haftbell Blow
description: Turn the bit at the last moment to bite past a hard layer and into the softer part beneath.

name: Easing Heavyeye
description: Step clear along the line a falling target will lean so the body is never beneath it.

name: Poleshoe Wedge
description: Drop the head across the front of the body to catch a heavy swing from above like a fallen beam.

name: Warm Wideswell
description: Read the lean of the opponent's shoulders to see which way the next blow will fall.

name: Narrow Rend
description: Time the exhale with the downward chop so a thin pulse of qi follows the bit into the target.

name: Rendbump
description: Release a long exhale through the whole swing so qi and breath both finish at the impact.

name: Measured Greatpoll
description: Draw slow breaths and let qi gather along the edge until the bit feels heavier in the hands.

name: Angled Longhelve
description: Inhale as the haft rises across the body and let a little qi stiffen the shaft against a blow.

name: Swaying Doubleedge
description: Step on the exhale and let qi lighten the leading leg for one smooth advance.

name: Timberreview
description: Hold a steady guard and track the opponent's breathing with a thread of qi along the haft.

name: Hard Greatbeard
description: Swing the curved edge through a rising arc so the whole crescent meets the target at once.

name: Greatstrike
description: Let the crescent edge swing back along the same arc after a cut to strike a second time.

name: Flat Riven
description: Thrust the sharp horn of the crescent bit forward to puncture a gap in the opponent's armor.

name: Towing Wideswell
description: Catch the opponent's weapon or shield rim with the lower beard of the bit and pull it off line.

name: Greatpause
description: Turn the flat of the crescent against an incoming blade and slide it away from the body.

name: Light Hewfall
description: Step along the line of the swing's arc so the body travels with the head instead of against it.

name: Haftbell Gauge
description: Send qi along the curve of the bit to feel how near the opponent stands before swinging.

name: Greatbit Dash
description: Open the stance and send a long flat swing across the full width of the target's front.

name: Open Hewfall
description: Extend both arms along the haft and swing the bit at the farthest reach of the stance.

name: Stepping Longhelve
description: Lean the body back out of a swing's reach and recover the stance with a short step.

name: Timberstay
description: Sweep the haft across the body in a long arc to push aside a low attack.

name: Soft Heavyeye
description: Watch the gaps in the opponent's stance to find where a wide cleave would land.

name: Rooted Rend
description: Sink qi into the legs and chop so the whole body stays rooted behind the falling bit.

name: Timbercowl
description: Drive qi into the lead foot and plant it so a heavy blow cannot push the body back.

name: Kind Haftrope
description: Let circulating qi sink to the lower body and steady the stance before a heavy stroke.

name: Backward Riven
description: Drag the rear foot after the front foot to close distance while the stance stays low.

name: Greatblow
description: Chop at the opponent's lead leg to break the root of their stance and unbalance them.

name: Judging Haftrope
description: Read through the ground and the haft how the opponent's weight moves between their feet.

name: Low Splitmass
description: Jab the middle of the haft forward into the opponent's chest or throat at close range.

name: Rivenstrike
description: Spin the haft in both hands and strike with the butt end on the far side.

name: Square Sunder
description: Slide both hands apart along the haft mid-swing to lengthen the cut by a hand's breadth.

name: Axestay
description: Sweep the shaft across the front of the body to knock away a low strike.

name: Rivenhusk
description: Catch an opponent's weapon between the haft and the head and twist it from their grip.

name: Turning Longhelve
description: Press the haft flat against the opponent's body and shove them back off balance.

name: Skipping Doubleedge
description: Roll the haft across the forearms and step backward in a controlled retreat from a close fight.

name: Axereview
description: Feel the shaft tremble in the hands and read the force and direction of the opponent's push.

name: Straight Wideswell
description: Send qi along the full length of the edge and chop so the whole bit bites at once.

name: Greatbit Hit
description: Draw the edge across the target from the heel of the bit to its toe in one drawing cut.

name: Timberhusk
description: Hold the edge upright before the face with qi in the steel to stop a descending blade.

name: Timbergauge
description: Run qi up the spine and out through the arms so the swing gains a little force.

name: Swaying Rend
description: Step along the line the edge will travel so the body arrives at the target as the cut does.

name: Greatreview
description: Listen to the hum of the edge through the haft to feel the true line of the swing.
